name: Blind Quality Metric
description: Computes no-reference (blind) image quality metrics using Natural Scene Statistics (NSS). Authentic photographs conform to well-established NSS models, while AI-generated images and manipulated regions exhibit systematic deviations from these natural statistical regularities.
algorithm: BLIINDS-II / BRISQUE-derived NSS Feature Extraction + SVR Quality Prediction
mechanism:
Blind image quality assessment operates without a pristine reference image by exploiting the fact that natural images occupy a tiny subspace of all possible pixel arrangements, governed by predictable statistical regularities.

The algorithm extracts Natural Scene Statistics (NSS) features from the Mean Subtracted Contrast Normalized (MSCN) coefficient domain. For each local patch, MSCN coefficients are computed as: Î(x,y) = (I(x,y) - μ(x,y)) / (σ(x,y) + C), where μ and σ are local mean and standard deviation. In natural images, these coefficients follow a Generalized Gaussian Distribution (GGD) with predictable shape and variance parameters.

AI-generated images violate NSS in characteristic ways: (1) their MSCN coefficient distributions deviate from the expected GGD shape — typically showing heavier tails or sharper peaks, (2) the pairwise products of adjacent MSCN coefficients fail to follow the expected Asymmetric Generalized Gaussian Distribution (AGGD), and (3) the multi-scale NSS features (computed at multiple downsampling levels) show inconsistent quality degradation patterns unlike natural optical blur.

The extracted NSS feature vector (typically 36-dimensional) is fed to a Support Vector Regression (SVR) model trained on human quality judgments to produce an interpretable quality/authenticity score.
parameters:
MSCN patch size: 7×7 Gaussian window
GGD fitting: moment-matching for shape parameter α
AGGD features: 4 directional pairwise products (H, V, D1, D2)
Scale levels: 2 (original + 2× downsampled)
Feature dimension: 36 (BRISQUE) or 24 (BLIINDS-II)
Classifier: SVR with RBF kernel
accuracy: Moderate — 68-80% accuracy for AI detection. Originally designed for quality assessment, forensic accuracy depends on how well the NSS deviation correlates with generation artifacts.
source: Saad, M.A. et al. (2012). Blind Image Quality Assessment: A Natural Scene Statistics Approach in the DCT Domain. IEEE TIP.
useCase: Forensic screening of suspected AI-generated images by measuring deviation from natural scene statistics, quality consistency verification across image regions to detect local manipulation, and baseline quality assessment in multi-method detection pipelines.
strengths:
• Grounded in decades of vision science research on Natural Scene Statistics
• No reference image required — applicable to any standalone image
• The NSS framework captures fundamental statistical properties that are extremely difficult for generators to perfectly replicate
• Multi-scale analysis catches artifacts at different spatial frequencies
limitations:
• AI generators are increasingly trained to match NSS distributions, reducing detection gap
• Highly compressed or heavily post-processed authentic images can violate NSS, causing false positives
• The SVR model requires retraining as new generator architectures emerge
• Performance degrades significantly on images smaller than 256×256 pixels

references.title: Saad, M.A. et al. (2012). Blind Image Quality Assessment: A Natural Scene Statistics Approach in the DCT Domain. IEEE TIP.
Mittal, A. et al. (2012). No-Reference Image Quality Assessment in the Spatial Domain (BRISQUE). IEEE TIP.
